item.text: {"search_note":"I found no 2024 reporting that Thailand under Srettha had a military operation, cross-border intervention, or declared conflict in which civilian harm or illegal conduct later required public accountability. I also found no evidence that Srettha had to retract a conflict justification, accept blame for military abuses, or explain contradictions between stated and actual wartime conduct. So the best-supported conclusion is limited: the public record shows restraint and humanitarian management, but there is no direct accountability episode to score against this lens in 2024.","evidence":[{"title":"Summary of Weekly Press Briefing 19 April 2024 at 11.00 hrs.","publisher":"Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand","date":"April 19, 2024","url":"https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/weeklypressbriefing190424-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e","summary":"Thailand said it was monitoring the Myanmar situation closely, created a special committee, and remained open to dialogue with stakeholders. That is evidence of a controlled public response rather than evasion of responsibility or cover-up.","question_ids":["2B.9","2B.5","2B.1"]},{"title":"ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Statement on the Escalation of Conflicts in Myanmar","publisher":"Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand","date":"April 18, 2024","url":"https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/asean-fm-statement-escalation-conflicts-myanmar?menu=5d5bd3dc15e39c306002ab1c&page=5d5bd3cb15e39c306002a9ac","summary":"ASEAN called for immediate restraint, cessation of violence, and civilian protection, and Thailand joined that line.
